coverage: overnight since last evening's brief (~19:30 Mon to ~08:15 Tue)
headline: Washington is holding up Patriot interceptors for Kyiv, including ones Europe already paid for; Alberta votes 76% to stay in Canada; France imposes curfews and Italy sends troops to Milan; Berlin signs an AI pact with Nvidia; Asia slides ahead of the AI earnings week.

stories.title: Washington is holding up Patriot interceptors for Kyiv, including missiles Europeans already paid for
facts: Washington Post: Defense Secretary Hegseth hasn't rejected the transfers but hasn't completed the steps needed to approve them.
Some of the stalled handoffs come from allied countries, which need his sign-off; he keeps approving other US aid (WaPo via Anadolu).
Zelensky told US senators Monday the Pentagon is delaying missiles Europeans paid for under NATO's PURL scheme; they await Hegseth's signature (Guardian).
Zelensky to Bloomberg on Oct 18: the US now supplies about 12 Patriot interceptors a month, roughly a quarter of the Biden-era rate (Kyiv Independent).
A Ukrainian official told the Post last week Kyiv had only "a couple" of Patriot interceptors left.
stories.whyItMatters: This follows Sunday night's strikes that cut power to 550,000 homes: without interceptors Ukraine has little defence against Russian ballistic missiles, and the delay is now coming from Washington, not from production.

image.alt: Trump administration delays approval of Patriot missiles for Ukraine: Report

stories.title: Alberta votes about 76 to 24 to stay in Canada
facts: CBC News projects a "remain" win; with more than 1 million votes counted, 76.6% chose remain and 23.5% the referendum path.
The ballot didn't ask about independence directly: option 2 would have started the legal process toward a binding separation vote (AP).
It was one of 10 questions; the five on immigration and four on constitutional changes were still being counted.
AP calls it a win for PM Mark Carney amid Trump's trade war and annexation threats; Premier Danielle Smith had said she'd vote remain.
stories.whyItMatters: It takes the separatist path off the table for now, though CBC notes polls suggested a slight majority of Smith's own UCP voters backed it.

via.label: The New York Times on X

stories.title: France imposes local curfews after the riots, and Italy sends soldiers into Milan
facts: Paris: no one may enter or stay on Place de la République or in Les Halles from 23:00 to 06:00 (BBC, AP).
Lyon put a large part of the Presqu'île under curfew from 21:00; Nice bars unaccompanied minors from its centre 21:00–06:00 until Oct 25 (RTL).
Lille, Douai, Wattignies and Denain: curfew for minors only in parts of town, 20:00–06:00 on Monday and Tuesday (franceinfo).
Paris is ruling out a state of emergency for now and opting for "partial and localised" curfews instead (RTL).
Italy: Milan's luxury shops closed as the government prepares to deploy troops; Bild reports 500 soldiers (Guardian, Bild).
stories.whyItMatters: Pepperstone's Chris Weston wrote in a note quoted by Reuters that French sovereign risk is now priced into European equities, so the unrest is starting to show up in markets too.

image.alt: Police stop a vehicle entering the curfew zone after 9 p.m. on Rue de la Barre, just before Place Bellecour in Lyon, France

stories.title: Berlin signs a physical-AI pact with Nvidia as Merz opens the Invest in Germany summit
facts: The economy and research ministries signed a joint declaration of intent with Nvidia to build advanced AI models for robots and industry (tagesschau, Nvidia).
About a dozen German firms are set to take part, including Siemens, Audi and Black Forest Labs (deutschland.de).
Nvidia also plans investments in Agile Robots, Avelios Medical, Mirelo and Reflex Aerospace.
Berlin named no budget; tagesschau cites a media report of a three-digit-million sum, partly to rent compute in Deutsche Telekom's AI cloud.
Huang says Nvidia invested almost $1 billion in Germany last year; the two-day summit with ~200 CEOs continues today.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the headline deal of a summit meant to pull private capital into Germany, but so far it's a declaration of intent with no public price tag.

stories.title: Asia slides before a big week of AI earnings; Brent near $110
facts: Reuters: Kospi −3.61%, Nikkei −1.28%, MSCI Asia ex-Japan −0.93% on Tuesday.
DAX futures −0.40%, Euro Stoxx 50 futures −0.71%; the euro sits at $1.12.
Meta reports Wednesday, then Tesla, Lam Research and Texas Instruments; Reuters says SpaceX results are due Tuesday.
Bloomberg (via TechCrunch): Nscale and Anthropic are in talks on a ~$45B cloud deal for a second Monarch building in West Virginia.
stories.whyItMatters: Expectations for AI hardware are high (BNP Paribas AM's Daniel Morris says the sector is expected to double its earnings), so this week's reports carry a lot of weight.

stories.title: OpenAI says its GPT-6 models can now migrate COBOL with up to 97.9% accuracy
facts: New in-house COBOL migration eval: GPT-6.1 Sol hits 86.6% at low reasoning effort vs 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 97.9% at higher effort.
MultiLangBench (build a SQLite-compatible engine in 20 languages): GPT-6 Astra 87.4% average pass rate vs 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol.
COBOL is still the hardest language for Astra at 72.1%; OCaml 85.8%, Fortran 83.5%, Visual Basic 89.4%.
GPT-6 Luna reaches 40.3% at about $0.77 per sample vs $3.48 for GPT-5.6 Sol.
OpenAI is publishing the MultiLangBench setup and test suite on GitHub; it says production use still needs expert review.
stories.whyItMatters: Legacy code in banking and government is a big enterprise market, and both benchmarks are OpenAI's own, so outside replication will matter.

image.alt: OpenAI card for its post on coding in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, OCaml, Fortran and Visual Basic

facts.text: Berlin: SPD board (26:3) and Greens (43 of 45 delegates) back coalition talks with Die Linke; Linke members decide on Oct 31.
Deutsche Bank and Linde end their business relationship after a fight over Russia gas-project guarantees.
Head of the doctors' association (Kassenärzte) Gassen warns public-insurance patients will wait even longer for appointments from next year because of the reform.
Japan's MMX mission launched toward Mars' moon Phobos with the rover "Idefix" aboard; it aims to bring a sample back.
Australian MP Helen Haines was reportedly hit twice by an SUV and may have lost a leg; attacks on politicians are very rare there.

image.alt: An artist's impression of the MMX spacecraft - which is a gold and black spacecraft with large solar panels, thrusters and antenna - flies above the red surface of Mars, which looms large in the background. It is heading towards the small, dark and irregularly shaped moon called Phobos.

facts.text: Go 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 are out with one standard-library security fix.
Meta publishes a technical report on Muse Glimmer, a 30B open-weight agent model that runs on a single consumer GPU at 4-bit.
Notion AI upgrade: more capable agents, bring-your-own AI keys, an improved Notion MCP and a new credit system.
Anthropic is promoting OSS Scanner again (launched Oct 8): free, opt-in, model-generated vuln scans with PoCs and patches for critical OSS projects.

image.alt: OSS Scanner, from the Frontier Red Team: free, periodic security scans for open-source projects by Anthropic.

facts.text: 49ers beat the Commanders 23–17 on Monday Night Football after building a big lead and holding on.
SPOX: San Francisco stays the NFL's only unbeaten team.
Washington WR Terry McLaurin appeared to suffer a serious left knee injury in the first quarter at Levi's Stadium.
